related_questions.question: What are the signs of prostate cancer getting worse?

text_blocks.snippet: Signs of worsening prostate cancer include increased pain (especially in the back, hips, or pelvis), difficulty urinating, blood in the urine or semen, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue. Advanced prostate cancer may also lead to bone pain, swelling in the lower body, and even nerve-related symptoms like numbness or weakness in the legs or feet.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased pain (especially in the back, hips, or pelvis), difficulty urinating, blood in the urine or semen, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue

list.snippet: Increased frequency of urination: Needing to urinate more often, especially at night.
Difficulty starting or stopping urination: Trouble initiating the flow of urine or maintaining a steady stream.
Pain or burning during urination: Discomfort or a burning sensation while urinating.
Blood in the urine or semen: Presence of blood in the urine or semen is a serious symptom that requires immediate medical attention.

list.title: Bone pain:
list.snippet: Pain in the bones, particularly the back, hips, pelvis, or ribs, is a common sign of prostate cancer spreading to the bones.

list.title: Swelling in the lower body:
list.snippet: Swelling in the legs or feet can occur if cancer compresses nearby lymph nodes or blood vessels.

list.title: Persistent pain in the pelvic or rectal area:
list.snippet: Pain or stiffness in the lower back, hips, pelvic or rectal area, or upper thighs.
Unexplained weight loss: Significant weight loss without trying to lose weight.
Fatigue and weakness: Feeling unusually tired or weak, even after resting.
Erectile dysfunction: Difficulty getting or maintaining an erection.
Numbness or weakness in the legs or feet: Numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs or feet, potentially due to spinal cord compression.
Changes in bowel or bladder control: Difficulty controlling bowel movements or urination.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: Some of these symptoms can also be caused by other, less serious conditions. However, it is crucial to consult with a doctor if you experience any of these symptoms, especially if they are persistent or worsening. Early detection and treatment are vital for managing prostate cancer effectively.

related_questions.question: How long can a man live with untreated prostate cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: The life expectancy for a man with untreated prostate cancer varies significantly based on several factors, primarily the stage and grade of the cancer, age, and overall health. Some men with very low-risk, localized prostate cancer may never require treatment and live a normal lifespan, while others with more aggressive, advanced cancers face a considerably shorter life expectancy.
snippet_highlighted_words: Some men with very low-risk, localized prostate cancer may never require treatment and live a normal lifespan, while others with more aggressive, advanced cancers face a considerably shorter life expectancy

list.title: Stage and Grade:
list.snippet: Prostate cancer is staged based on its extent within the prostate and surrounding areas, and graded based on how abnormal the cancer cells appear under a microscope. Low-grade cancers tend to grow slowly, while high-grade cancers are more aggressive and prone to spreading.

list.title: Age and Health:
list.snippet: Older men and those with other health conditions may have a shorter overall life expectancy, even if their prostate cancer is well-managed.

list.title: Patient Preferences:
list.snippet: Treatment decisions are also influenced by the patient's values and preferences, including their willingness to accept the potential side effects of treatment versus the risks of watchful waiting.

list.title: Localized Prostate Cancer (Early Stages):
list.snippet: For men with early-stage, localized prostate cancer, survival rates can be very high, even with no treatment, as the cancer may grow slowly or not at all. Some studies show 5-year survival rates approaching 100% for early stages.

list.title: Advanced Prostate Cancer:
list.snippet: In contrast, advanced prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic cancer) has a significantly lower survival rate, often around 5 to 6 years on average after diagnosis according to MD Anderson Cancer Center.

list.title: Disease-Specific Survival:
list.snippet: Even with untreated prostate cancer, some men may die from other causes, while others may succumb to the cancer itself. Disease-specific survival rates focus on how many men die from prostate cancer, regardless of other causes of death.

list.title: Active Surveillance:
list.snippet: Some men with low-risk prostate cancer may opt for active surveillance, which involves regular monitoring of the cancer and delaying treatment until there are signs of progression. This approach can be successful, but it requires careful monitoring and a high degree of patient compliance.

list.title: Individualized Prognosis:
list.snippet: It is crucial to remember that survival rates are averages and do not predict individual outcomes. The best way to understand the prognosis for a specific individual is to consult with a healthcare professional who can assess the unique characteristics of their cancer and overall health.

related_questions.question: What happens if prostate cancer is left untreated?

text_blocks.snippet: If left untreated, prostate cancer can lead to a variety of complications, including pain, urinary and bowel problems, and in advanced stages, it can spread to other parts of the body, potentially becoming life-threatening. While some prostate cancers grow slowly and may not cause significant issues, others can progress more rapidly and require treatment.
snippet_highlighted_words: can lead to a variety of complications, including pain, urinary and bowel problems, and in advanced stages, it can spread to other parts of the body, potentially becoming life-threatening

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the potential consequences:

list.title: Tumor Growth:
list.snippet: Untreated prostate cancer can grow, potentially invading nearby tissues and structures like the seminal vesicles, bladder, or rectum.

list.title: Urinary and Bowel Issues:
list.snippet: The growing tumor can put pressure on the urethra, leading to difficulty emptying the bladder, frequent urination, or a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying. It can also cause constipation or changes in bowel habits.

list.title: Pain:
list.snippet: Pain, particularly in the pelvic area, lower back, or thighs, can develop as the cancer progresses.

list.title: Bone Metastasis:
list.snippet: Prostate cancer has a tendency to spread to the bones, especially the spine, pelvis, and femur. This can cause significant pain, fractures, and other complications.

list.title: Other Metastatic Sites:
list.snippet: While less common, prostate cancer can also spread to the liver, lungs, or brain. Metastasis to these organs can lead to various issues like liver failure, lung collapse, or neurological problems.

list.title: Reduced Quality of Life:
list.snippet: Untreated prostate cancer, especially in advanced stages, can significantly impact a person's quality of life due to pain, urinary and bowel dysfunction, and other complications.

list.title: Decreased Life Expectancy:
list.snippet: While some prostate cancers are slow-growing and may not impact lifespan, advanced, metastatic prostate cancer can be life-threatening and lead to a shortened life expectancy.

list.title: Systemic Effects:
list.snippet: In advanced stages, prostate cancer can lead to malnutrition, muscle wasting, fatigue, and increased susceptibility to infections.

list.title: Not All Prostate Cancers Are Aggressive:
list.snippet: Some prostate cancers are slow-growing and may not require immediate treatment. Doctors often use a "watchful waiting" approach for these cases, monitoring the cancer's progression and intervening only if it starts to grow or cause symptoms.

list.title: Treatment Options Exist:
list.snippet: Even if prostate cancer has spread, there are treatments like hormone therapy and chemotherapy that can help manage the disease and improve quality of life.

list.title: Palliative Care:
list.snippet: For those with advanced prostate cancer, palliative care can help manage symptoms and improve comfort, even if a cure is not possible.

key_moments.title: Some people may know someone who died young from prostate cancer, and so they may doubt the optimistic outlook that these numbers suggest. There are two situations in which a person would die unusually young from prostate cancer. First, a man may not be screening and so he would not be diagnosed and treated until the disease is at an advanced stage. Second, some men have rare forms of the disease that are especially aggressive and difficult to treat.
